name: implied_vs_realized_vol_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: India VIX (implied vol) systematically overestimates realized NIFTY volatility by 3-5 vol points on average -- the variance risk premium (VRP). When VIX spikes to >2 standard deviations above its 20-day mean but realized 5-day vol hasn't increased proportionally, the VRP is elevated and NIFTY tends to mean-revert (as the implied fear dissipates). The strategy goes long via BUY_CE on NIFTY50 index options when VRP is extreme, betting that realized vol will remain below implied, and the fear premium will compress. The inefficiency persists because the VRP in Indian markets is structurally higher than developed markets (fewer hedging alternatives, concentrated retail option selling), and retail traders cannot easily trade the VRP directly.
indicators: RV_5d = realized_vol(NIFTY_returns, lookback=5_days) * sqrt(252)  # annualized 5-day realized vol
VRP = VIX - RV_5d  # variance risk premium in vol points
VRP_z = (VRP - SMA(VRP, 20_days)) / rolling_std(VRP, 20_days)  # z-score of VRP
VIX_rate_of_change_720 = (VIX - VIX[720]) / VIX[720] * 100  # VIX % change in last hour (720 bars at 5s)

conditions: VRP_z > 2.0 (VRP is unusually high -- implied vol overpricing fear)
VIX_z > 1.5 (VIX elevated relative to recent history)
VIX_rate_of_change_720 > 5 (VIX spiked recently, likely to revert)
NIFTY_RSI_360 < 40 (market pulled back, creating entry opportunity)
long.confirmation: VIX starts declining (VIX[t] < VIX[t-12]) for 12 bars (60 seconds) while NIFTY stabilizes

conditions: VRP_z < -1.5 (VRP collapsed -- implied vol under-pricing risk)
short.confirmation: VIX starts rising (VIX[t] > VIX[t-12]) for 12 bars (60 seconds) while NIFTY stalls

entry.entry_price: market order on NIFTY50 ATM CE/PE

exit.target: VRP_z returns to 0.5 (VRP normalizing) OR option premium gains 0.5% from entry
exit.stop_loss: VRP_z exceeds 3.5 (VRP widening further -- true risk event) OR option premium drops 0.5% from entry
exit.trailing_stop: after 0.3% gain, trail at 0.15% below highest premium
exit.time_stop: exit after 12 bars (60 seconds) if no progress
exit.signal_exit: if VIX makes new session high while in BUY_CE position, exit (fear escalating)

risk.position_sizing: VIX-adjusted: base_size * (18 / VIX) -- reduce size when VIX is high

filters.vix_filter: core of strategy -- requires VIX > 15 for long signals (VRP meaningful only at elevated levels)
filters.time_filter: signal can trigger any time; prefer morning entry for maximum session time remaining
filters.volume_filter: NIFTY option volume must be > avg (confirming VIX is liquid/accurate)
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY not in circuit-breaker territory or limit-down
filters.event_filter: skip on RBI policy day, elections, budget (VIX spikes are justified on these days)
other_filters: skip if realized vol is also spiking (VRP high because RV is low, not because IV is high)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low -- VRP is a structural risk premium that has persisted globally for decades

mechanism: At 5-second frequency, the VRP signal itself is slow-moving (daily-scale), but the ENTRY TIMING precision is critical. The 12-bar (60-second) VIX confirmation window at 5s granularity detects the exact moment when VIX starts to turn after a spike -- this is when option premiums are still elevated but about to compress. Buying CE/PE at this inflection captures the initial premium adjustment that happens in 5-30 seconds as market makers reprice. The 5s bar allows detecting VIX micro-reversals invisible on 1-min charts, giving a 10-30 second head start on premium repricing.
adaptation_notes: Adapted from 1-min equity/ETF strategy to 5-sec index option strategy. Key changes: (1) Universe changed from NIFTYBEES/top-5 stocks to NIFTY50 ATM index options (BUY_CE/BUY_PE), (2) RSI lookback adjusted from 30 bars (30 min) to 360 bars (30 min at 5s), (3) VIX rate of change adjusted from 60 bars to 720 bars (equivalent 1 hour at 5s), (4) VIX confirmation changed from 5-bar 1-min to 12-bar 5s (60 seconds), (5) Hold time compressed from 60-300 minutes to 5-60 seconds -- scalping the initial VRP compression in option premium, (6) Entry/exit now reference option premium (BUY_CE/BUY_PE) instead of equity BUY/SHORT, (7) Removed stock_filter as we trade index options directly.
weaknesses: Low signal frequency: VRP_z > 2.0 occurs only 5-10 times per month, making this a supplement strategy, not a standalone
The strategy is essentially long NIFTY via CE on pullbacks with a VIX filter -- during genuine bear markets, VIX spikes ARE justified and the strategy will lose on multiple consecutive signals
Intraday VRP calculation is noisy because India VIX can be stale (updated every few minutes, not truly real-time), causing false signals
prior_art: Carr & Wu (2009) variance risk premia; Bollerslev et al. (2009) expected stock returns and variance risk premia. Indian VRP studied by Sehgal & Vijayakumar (2008).
notes: Adapted for 5-second NIFTY50 index option trading. Edge math: 0.62 * 50bps - 0.38 * 35bps = 31 - 13.3 = 17.7bps gross per signal day.
